name: Argentina
summary: Three mobile networks - Claro, Personal and Movistar - but Telecom Argentina (Personal) has owned Movistar (TMA) since Feb 2025; the antitrust tribunal approved the deal in June 2026 on condition of divesting 6 million customers with spectrum, not yet done. 700/AWS/3.5 GHz are national; 850/1900 are licensed in three areas and 900/2.6 GHz by locality.

operators.name: Personal
operators.notes: Telecom Argentina's mobile brand. Absorbed Nextel Argentina's 900 MHz and 2.5 GHz rights via the Cablevisión-Telecom merger (2018). Owner of Movistar Argentina (TMA) since 24 Feb 2025.

operators.name: Movistar
operators.notes: Acquired by Telecom Argentina from Telefónica on 24 Feb 2025 and run as a separate network segment. On 17 Jun 2026 the Antitrust Tribunal (ANC) conditioned the deal on divesting at least 6 million mobile customers (4m AMBA, 2m rest of country) with the spectrum needed to serve them, plus 211,400 home-internet lines; as of Aug 2026 no buyer or spectrum package had been chosen.

blocks.notes: New-entrant lot 1 (awarded to Arlink S.A. in 2014); current holder/status not verified

bands.note: EU 800 plan not used (conflicts with APT 700 and 850). 806-824 MHz was Nextel trunking spectrum; not compiled.

bands.label: 850 MHz (B5)
bands.note: Licensed in three areas (AMBA, Norte, Sur), non-expiring. AMBA: Movistar 2x15, Personal 2x10 (incl. 830.25-834/875.25-879 from 2014). Norte: Personal 2x12.5, Claro 2x12.5. Sur: Movistar 2x12.5, Claro 2x12.5. After Telecom's purchase of TMA, Telecom controls all of 850 MHz in AMBA.

bands.note: 905-915/950-960 MHz was allocated to mobile in 2017 (ENACOM Res. 1,033-E/17) and assigned to Nextel (now Telecom/Personal) by locality under a refarming project. The rest of 880-960 is not mobile. América Movil also lists 900 MHz for Claro Argentina - not confirmed, possibly 850 MHz.

Sur: Personal 2x25, Movistar 2x12.5, Claro 2x12.5 (holdings plus the 2014 remnant lots). The remaining 2x10 per area was the 2014 new-entrant lot (status not verified).

bands.label: 2.5 GHz FDD (B7)
bands.note: Assigned per locality (ENACOM Res. 5,478-E/17, 15 years): Lot A (3 FDD channels) Movistar, Lot B (3 FDD channels) Claro, Lot C (2 FDD + 4 TDD channels) Personal, plus Nextel's refarmed channels 7-12 (2530-2560/2650-2680) now Personal. Amounts are those held in licensed localities (CABA, provincial capitals, Rosario, Mar del Plata, Bahía Blanca...), not population-weighted, so totals overstate. Telefónica reports Movistar's 2x15 covers 65% of the population, expiring 2035. Personal's current 2.5 GHz amounts after the 2018 Cablevisión merger were not re-confirmed.

bands.label: 3.3-3.6 GHz (n78)
bands.note: Oct 2023 5G auction: ENACOM states Lot 1 3300–3400 Claro, Lot 2 3400–3500 Telecom (Personal), Lot 3B 3550–3600 Telefónica (Movistar); one 50 MHz lot unsold. ENACOM Res. 611/2025 cut the per-group cap from 200 to 150 MHz, so Telecom's combined 150 MHz is at the cap. Terms to 2043.

notes: ENACOM's website was unreachable while compiling (TLS/503), so no regulator document could be checked; all figures come from the operators' SEC filings (Telecom Argentina 20-F FY2014/FY2018/FY2025, Telefónica S.A. 20-F FY2024, América Movil 20-F FY2025) and Telecom's 2026 6-K reports.
Area shares used for averages (AMBA/Norte/Sur ~32/41/27% of population) are approximate and from background knowledge, not source-verified.

Telecom Argentina bought 99.99% of Telefónica Móviles Argentina (TMA) on 24 Feb 2025. The Secretary of Industry and Commerce ordered a hold-separate (Resolution 63/2025, later suspended by the courts). The ANC's Antitrust Tribunal approved it with conditions on 17 Jun 2026 (RESFC-2026-38-APN-TDC#ANC): transfer 6m mobile customers and 'the rights of use of radio spectrum ... necessary for the competitive operation of the divested mobile service'. As of the H1 2026 report (Aug 2026) no buyer or spectrum package had been chosen, so no future-dated entry could be drawn.
Movistar and Personal are shown separately because they still hold separate licences and run separate networks; both are controlled by Telecom Argentina.
América Movil's 20-F describes a Nov 2023 ENACOM Res. 2023-1473 award as '2.6 GHz 5G band'; the timing and amount match the 3.5 GHz auction, so it is treated as Claro's 3.5 GHz lot.
Corrected after independent verification (2026-09-28): 3.5 GHz edges confirmed by ENACOM's own announcement plus DPL News; upgraded to verified.
